title: The Relay pattern discards the two refusal facts its own API returns, shows no tenant/scope, cannot be cancelled, and announces nothing to a screen reader
why_open:
The chat route already produces the facts the Relay surface is required to show and the panel throws both away. apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:143-156 returns `aiDisabledReason` (this tenant switched the assistant off, with the flag's own reason) and `toolRefusal` (this principal may not run `search.corpus`, or this system does not offer it) — the route's header comment at :48-51 states outright that collapsing the two 'would tell at least one person something false'. apps/web/src/components/ai/TenureAIPanel.tsx:72 types the response as `{ answer: string | null; aiEnabled: boolean; sources: Source[] }` only, so both fields are dropped on the floor, and the fallback ladder at :77-84 then tells a tenant that deliberately disabled the assistant "AI answers aren't set up for this workspace yet" and tells a user refused the retrieval tool "I couldn't find anything about that in your workspace" — a false statement about their own data. This is a defect and not house style: the sibling AI surface apps/web/src/components/DraftAssist.tsx:33-41 already distinguishes 403 (flag off) from 503 (no model) in its copy. Three further clauses of Bible §10 have no implementation. (a) 'It always shows tenant, active scope and sources it may use' — the panel header at :119-126 says only 'Grounded in your workspace', the component takes no props at all, and apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:97 renders `` bare although that same file already holds `tenants.active` (:38-42). (b) 'allow cancellation' — `ask()` at :59-91 creates no AbortController and the only affordance while `loading` is a disabled send button (:226). (c) Announcements — `grep -rn 'aria-live|role="status"' src/components` returns no hit inside components/ai, so the assistant answer appended at :162-192 and the 'Tenure AI is thinking…' indicator at :194-198 arrive silently for a screen-reader user; the repo does this correctly elsewhere (apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx:86-92 uses role="alert" with a comment explaining why), and DraftAssist.tsx:77 renders its error as a bare `

` that only mounts after the failure, so it is unannounceable by construction.
smallest_real_change: Extract `relayReply({ answer, aiEnabled, aiDisabledReason, toolRefusal, sourceCount })` into a new pure module apps/web/src/components/ai/relay-reply.ts returning the message for the four distinguishable outcomes (answered / flag off, naming the reason / tool refused, naming the reason / no key configured), widen the fetch result type at TenureAIPanel.tsx:72 to include the two fields the route already sends, and call `relayReply` in place of the inline ladder at :77-84 — the panel is the production caller. Add a required `scope: { tenantName: string }` prop passed from apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:97 out of the `tenants.active` it already loads, rendered under the title in place of 'Grounded in your workspace'; every construction site of TenureAIPanel is that one line, so the prop cannot be silently unset. Hold an AbortController in `ask()` and render a Stop button while `loading` that aborts it and appends a cancelled turn. Wrap the transcript in a permanently-mounted `<div aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="false">` (mounted even when empty, or nothing is announced) and give DraftAssist an always-rendered `role="status"` container for its error text. Proof: (1) jest on relay-reply.ts — mutation: collapse the `toolRefusal` branch into the `aiEnabled` branch, the 'a refused user is not told the assistant is unconfigured' case must fail, restore, pass; (2) a Playwright case in apps/web/e2e/relay.spec.ts asserting the OPEN panel prints the seeded institution's name in its scope line and that the transcript container carries aria-live="polite" — both assertions read what the production path emits, so deleting the layout prop or the aria attribute reds them, which a test calling relayReply directly would not.

title: No owned chart frame exists — every chart ships without source, freshness, unit, metric definition, accessible table or export
why_open: Bible §11 requires all charts to sit in a shared frame carrying title, question, metric definition, source, freshness, filters, comparison, unit/currency, accessible table, export and drill-through. apps/web/src/components/charts/index.ts:1-21 exports the marks (LineArea/Bar/HBar/Donut/Sankey/Sparkline/Meter), a legend, a tooltip, an empty state and a range filter — there is no frame, and `grep -rn 'ChartFrame' src/` returns zero. Real callers therefore drop a bare mark into a generic Card: apps/web/src/components/charts/panels/ActivityChart.tsx:22-31 renders `<Card><CardHeader title="Activity" .../><LineAreaChart .../></Card>` with nothing saying which rows the count came from, as of when, or in what unit. The only freshness affordance in the whole kit is apps/web/src/components/charts/LiveStats.tsx:49 ('Updated {ago}'), which no chart uses. There is no accessible table alternative anywhere — `grep -rn '<table' src/components/charts` returns zero; the marks carry per-point aria-labels only (LineAreaChart.tsx:178-179, DonutChart.tsx:100-101, BarChart.tsx:156-157), which is a thirty-stop focus tour rather than a table a screen-reader user can read, and Bible §13 asks specifically for 'chart alternatives'. And there is no export at all: `grep -rn 'csv|CSV|download' src/components/charts src/app/(app)/reports` returns zero, so §11's export and §12's CSV-formula-injection rule have nothing to apply to.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/components/charts/ChartFrame.tsx taking `{ title, question, source, asOf, unit, columns, rows, children }`: it renders the header line (title + question + 'Source · as of' + unit) and a disclosure-toggled `<table>` with a `<caption>` and `scope="col"` headers built from the same `columns`/`rows` the mark is handed, plus a 'Download CSV' button. Put the row derivation and cell formatting in a pure apps/web/src/components/charts/chart-table.ts (`tableFromSeries(categories, series)` and `csvCell(value)`), so the CSV rule is unit-testable: `csvCell` must prefix a leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR with an apostrophe (Bible §12, CSV formula injection). Adopt the frame in ActivityChart.tsx — it already computes `days` at :16-19, so `columns` and `rows` are free — and in one reports surface. Proof: (1) jest on chart-table.ts — mutation: drop the apostrophe prefix in `csvCell`, the `=1+1` case fails, restore, pass; (2) a Playwright case asserting the dashboard's Activity chart exposes a table whose cell values equal the plotted values — mutation: remove the `<table>` branch from ChartFrame, red. Do NOT touch src/components/finance/* here; a concurrent run owns the finance path.

title: No token pipeline and no type generation — one flat semantic layer of raw hex, and the token list is hand-copied into three files that nothing checks against each other
why_open: Bible §4 requires `primitive → semantic → component → tenant-safe overrides` compiled to CSS custom properties AND typed TypeScript. What exists is one flat layer of literals: apps/web/src/app/globals.css:24-166 declares the semantic names directly as hex (`:38 --primary: #198052`, `:65 --border: #e6e4dd`, `:71 --text-1: #191a1c`), and `grep -c 'tenure-forest|tenure-neutral' src/app/globals.css` returns 0 — there is no primitive scale for a semantic token to reference, so 'change the brand ramp' is a find-and-replace across 674 lines. There is no type generation of any kind: `grep -rn 'style-dictionary|tokens.json|designTokens'` across apps/web/src, tools, packages and tests hits only ledger prose. The one file that reads the real tokens, apps/web/src/lib/a11y/theme-tokens.ts, is a node-only test helper (`import fs from 'node:fs'` at :16) whose sole importer is apps/web/src/lib/a11y/contrast.test.ts:16 — nothing in the browser bundle can name a token in a type-checked way. Meanwhile the token list is hand-maintained in three places that nothing reconciles: globals.css:24-166, apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:19-76 (which re-declares every name as a `var(--x)` string, including the whole chart ramp at :65-76), and apps/web/src/components/charts/palette.ts:25-34 (a third copy of the eight `"var(--chart-N)"` strings). theme-tokens.ts:5-9 names this exact failure mode — 'a hand-maintained copy of the palette … passes the contrast audit forever while the stylesheet drifts underneath it' — and then it is what tailwind.config.ts is. Concretely: rename `--text-1` in globals.css and `text-text-1` silently resolves to an undefined custom property (text falls back to inherited colour) with every existing test still green.
smallest_real_change: Two halves, both small. (1) Introduce the primitive layer: add a `--tenure-forest-*` / `--tenure-neutral-*` ramp to the `:root` block of globals.css whose values are exactly the hexes the semantic tokens already carry, and rewrite the semantic declarations to `var(--tenure-…)`. `token()` in theme-tokens.ts:116-124 already follows `var(--other)` indirection, so contrast.test.ts keeps passing on identical resolved colours — that is the safety proof that this is a re-layering and not a repaint. (2) Add apps/web/src/lib/a11y/tokens.ts exporting the catalog as data — `{ name, layer: 'primitive'|'semantic'|'component' }[]` — plus `export type TokenName` (a union derived from it with `as const`) and `cssVar(name: TokenName): string`. Give it a real production caller: replace the eight literal strings in charts/palette.ts:25-34 with `cssVar('--chart-1')…`, so a token deleted from the catalog fails `tsc` at a rendering call site rather than at runtime. Test in tokens.test.ts using `readThemes()`: every catalog name resolves in all four themes; every `var(--x)` referenced by tailwind.config.ts is a catalog member; every custom property declared in globals.css is in the catalog (no undeclared token); and no `layer: 'semantic'` token resolves to a raw hex in its own declaration (it must reference a primitive). Mutations: rename `--text-1` in globals.css → the tailwind-reconciliation case fails; give one semantic token a literal hex again → the layering case fails. Note both globals.css and tailwind.config.ts sit outside src/components — check `git status --porcelain` before staging, since another cluster run may be in the same tree.

title: No owned grid contract — seven independently hand-rolled tables, none with a caption, column scope, sort, keyboard model or permission-aware cells
why_open: Bible §9 says 'Build one owned grid contract' and lists virtualization, keyboard cell/row navigation, sort/filter/group, saved views, selection and bulk actions, cell-level redaction, export preview and a mobile card alternative. `grep -rn 'DataGrid|DataTable' apps/web/src` returns zero. What ships is seven separate `<table>` elements written by hand, each with its own markup: apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/audit/page.tsx:170-178, apps/web/src/app/(app)/reports/finance/page.tsx:117, apps/web/src/components/finance/FinanceDashboard.tsx:175, apps/web/src/components/finance/LedgerDrawer.tsx:95, apps/web/src/components/finance/BudgetUpload.tsx:154, apps/web/src/components/documents/DocContentView.tsx:89 and apps/web/src/components/documents/DocumentViewerOverlay.tsx:502. The audit table is representative and is the densest surface in the product: `<thead><tr>` at :171-179 emits six bare `<th>` with no `scope="col"`, the table has no `<caption>`, no `aria-rowcount`, no sortable header and no keyboard model — so a screen-reader user in a 500-row audit log gets an unlabelled grid (WCAG 1.3.1), and Bible §9's 'do not expose a vendor grid API directly to domain code' has no Tenure-owned API to point domain code at in the first place.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/src/components/ui/DataTable.tsx: a typed `columns: Column<T>[]` / `rows: T[]` contract that emits `<table>` with a required `caption` (visually hidden by default), `<th scope="col">` for every column, `aria-sort` on sortable headers, and a `redact?: (row) => boolean` hook so a cell the viewer may not see renders a redaction marker rather than being absent (Bible §12: never leak forbidden object existence). Keep the sort comparator and the column-projection logic in a pure apps/web/src/components/ui/data-table-model.ts so it is unit-testable without a DOM (this repo's jest is `testEnvironment: 'node'` with no @testing-library, per apps/web/jest.config.js:9). Adopt it in exactly two callers to prove the contract carries real data: the audit log at admin/audit/page.tsx:169-200 and DocContentView.tsx:89. Proof: (1) jest on data-table-model.ts — mutation: make the sort comparator ignore the direction flag, the descending case fails; (2) a Playwright case asserting the audit table exposes `caption` text and that every `th` carries `scope="col"` — mutation: delete `scope` from DataTable's header cell, red. Two other runs are in this tree: do not touch src/components/finance/* or the approvals routes as part of this.

title: No long-session evidence and no frontline/touch evidence exist — one desktop Playwright project, a 24px target floor, and nothing that runs a session long enough to leak
why_open: `grep -rln 'long session|soak|memory leak' apps/web/e2e apps/web/src` returns nothing — there is no spec that keeps one session alive across a realistic working stretch, so nothing would catch a listener or detached-node leak in the shell, a growing transcript, or a session that silently expires and loses a draft mid-task (Bible §12: 'Session timeout/reauth preserves safe drafts without retaining secrets'; §18: 'perceived workload/comfort in representative long sessions'). Frontline is equally unevidenced: apps/web/playwright.config.ts:84 declares exactly one project — `[{ name: "chromium", use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"] } }]` — so no spec has ever run with `hasTouch` or at a tablet viewport, although Bible §15 makes tablet the review/approval/frontline device. The one target-size assertion that exists, apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:135, is titled 'nothing interactive is under 24px' and enforces the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum; Bible §4.6's frontline bar is 'touch controls at least 44 CSS px where required' and nothing checks it. Bible §6 'Critical flows never depend only on hover' is also unasserted (`grep -rn 'hover' apps/web/e2e` → no coverage). This one cannot honestly become PASS on automation alone — moderated usability sessions are human work — so the truthful outcome of the change below is the measurable half green and the human half recorded as the named residual, not a blanket PASS.
smallest_real_change: Two specs, no config change (use `test.use({ ...devices['iPad (gen 7)'] })` inside the frontline spec so the shared single-project config at playwright.config.ts:84 is left alone and other specs do not double-run). (1) apps/web/e2e/long-session.spec.ts: sign in once and drive one continuous session of ~30 real steps across dashboard → search → calendar → memory → messages → notifications with theme and nav-collapse toggles, asserting (a) zero console errors and zero page errors accumulated over the whole run, (b) `document.getElementsByTagName('*').length` measured after navigation 3 and after navigation 20 differs by less than a stated bound on the same route — a monotonic climb is the leak signature, (c) a draft typed into the message composer survives a forced re-auth (clear the session cookie, reload, sign in) rather than being lost. (2) apps/web/e2e/frontline-touch.spec.ts: at the tablet profile, walk the approve/capture path and assert every interactive control on it is ≥44 CSS px in both dimensions, reusing the `visibleInteractive` helper shape from a11y.spec.ts:23-51, and assert the primary actions on that path are reachable without hover (each has a focusable/clickable affordance while `page.emulateMedia({ forcedColors: 'none' })` and no pointer hover is issued). Mutations: shrink one primary control below 44px in the tablet path → the frontline case reds; remove the draft-restore assertion's re-auth step and it stops proving anything, so keep the re-auth in the assertion path. Record the moderated-usability half as the explicit residual in the ledger entry rather than claiming it.

title: The thirteen proving journeys are unproven — 31 feature-shaped specs, no journey-shaped spec, and only one seeded tenant to be 'materially different' from
why_open: Bible §19 names thirteen end-to-end journeys, each spanning several surfaces in one continuous session. apps/web/e2e holds 31 specs and every one is feature-shaped rather than journey-shaped — finance.spec.ts, calendar.spec.ts, messaging.spec.ts, handoff.spec.ts (whose two tests at :7 and :27 assert the handoff page 'assembles seats, predecessors, knowledge counts' and 'is reachable as a club tab', i.e. the page renders, not that a successor completed journey 9). Journeys with no coverage at all: 1 (first day: sign in → understand role → complete priorities → find help), 11 (permission denial → step-up → session expiry with no data loss or leak), 12 (themes + density + locale + RTL + zoom + high contrast + AT in one pass — apps/web/e2e/localization.spec.ts covers `lang`/`dir` only, at :16-40, and a11y.spec.ts covers criteria one at a time), 13 (the WRK missing-connection journey, which also has no Connection Center to drive). Personas do exist — `grep -rn 'signIn(page, "' e2e/*.spec.ts` shows five seeded accounts in use (Dana Whitfield 52, Priya Raman 29, Victor Chen 28, Maya Johnson 24, Isaiah Brooks 5) — but 'materially different tenants' has nothing to vary: apps/web/scripts/seed.mjs:78-84 upserts exactly one institution (`slug: "rochester"`), so no journey can be run twice against materially different tenant configurations today. Journeys 3–7 (finance close, HR effective-dated transaction, planner grid, operations scanner/offline, executive drill-through) address domains this application does not contain, and claiming them would be a false PASS.
smallest_real_change: Add apps/web/e2e/journeys.spec.ts containing one `test` per journey the product can actually support, each driven as a single continuous session across surfaces rather than as page assertions: journey 1 as Maya Johnson (sign in → dashboard priorities → open the first item → reach help), journey 2 as Priya Raman (inbox → open request → read consequences → decide → verify the record and the audit row both changed), journey 8 as Victor Chen (budget → request → event → document → handoff, in that order, one session), journey 9 as the incoming seat holder (successor briefing with at least one cited memory card opened from the briefing), journey 10 as the Relay path (ask → cite → open the cited record → confirm provenance survives), journey 11 (attempt a forbidden object, assert 404-not-403 and no existence leak, then expire the session mid-form and assert the draft survives), journey 12 (one pass toggling theme, density, high contrast and zoom while completing the same task). Put shared step helpers in apps/web/e2e/support/journeys.ts. In the same file, name journeys 3–7 and 13 as NOT_APPLICABLE / BLOCKED with the reason in a header comment — the HR, planning and operations domains are not built in apps/web, and journey 13 needs the WRK Connection Center (TTES-030-005) — so the file states its own coverage instead of implying thirteen. Record 'materially different tenants' as BLOCKED_EXTERNAL in the ledger naming the unblocking command: a second institution in apps/web/scripts/seed.mjs plus a re-seed, which sits outside this run's file allowlist. Mutation proof per journey: break one mid-journey step (e.g. remove the decision write in journey 2) and confirm the journey reds at that step rather than at its first assertion.

title: The tenant experience has no architecture document, and the one ownership document that exists says the tenant design system and the deployer console are the same shared thing
why_open: The gate asks that the tenant experience have a distinct DOCUMENTED architecture. The separation is real in code — apps/system-studio is a second Next.js app with its own deliberately-different palette (apps/system-studio/src/app/globals.css:1-17 explains it must not look like the product), and `grep -rn '@/lib/system|@/lib/provisioning|@tenure/blueprints' 'apps/web/src/app/(app)' apps/web/src/components` returns nothing, so no control-plane module leaks into a tenant surface today. But nothing documents or enforces it. docs/architecture holds no tenant-experience document: CURRENT-STATE-INVENTORY.md is a backend/infra inventory (its §1 is stack, ORM, RDS, ECS), PLATFORM-ARCHITECTURE.md and REVIEW-FINDINGS.md are the tenancy/RLS design, and the only mention of TTES anywhere in docs/architecture outside the registry is architecture-document-graph.yaml:491-503 listing the Bible as an input. Worse, the one ownership document actively contradicts Bible §1: tools/ownership-map.mjs:302-305 lists `apps/web/src/components/ui/`, `apps/web/src/components/shell/`, `apps/web/src/components/brand/` and `apps/system-studio/src/components/` under a single SHARED_PREFIXES bucket, and the generated docs/architecture/ownership.md:51-54 gives all four the identical reason 'the shell and the design system — what every domain renders through' — i.e. the repo's only ownership statement declares the tenant product and the operator console to be one design system, which is the exact merge §1 forbids. There is also a live false claim about the boundary: apps/web/playwright.config.ts:62-71 sets `PLATFORM_OPERATORS` 'so studio.spec.ts would [not] pass … for the wrong reason', but `find apps/web/e2e -iname '*studio*'` is empty and `grep -rn PLATFORM_OPERATORS apps/web/src` is empty — that spec and that gate live in apps/system-studio now, so the comment describes a file that is not there and the variable it sets is read by nothing in this app.
smallest_real_change: Write docs/architecture/TENANT-EXPERIENCE.md as the distinct architecture: the tenant shell (SkipLink → ShellHeader → SideNav → MainRegion → Footer → TenureAIPanel, as composed at apps/web/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx:73-99), the route table for every directory under apps/web/src/app/(app), the token layers and where they live, the owned-component inventory, and the boundary rules against apps/system-studio. Then enforce it in tests/architecture/tenant-experience-boundary.test.mjs, in the shape tests/architecture/ownership.test.mjs already uses: (a) no file under apps/web/src imports from apps/system-studio/src and no file under apps/system-studio/src imports from apps/web/src, in either direction; (b) every route directory under apps/web/src/app/(app) appears in the document's route table and every row of that table names a directory that exists — mutation: add a route directory and do not document it, the test must red, which is what makes the document load-bearing rather than a snapshot. Split SHARED_PREFIXES in tools/ownership-map.mjs:302-305 so `apps/system-studio/src/components/` carries its own reason ('the operator console's own shell — deliberately not the tenant design system') and regenerate docs/architecture/ownership.md via tools/ownership-map.mjs rather than editing the generated file. Finally correct the stale comment at apps/web/playwright.config.ts:62-71 and drop the `PLATFORM_OPERATORS` default there, or move it to apps/system-studio's own config where the spec it names actually lives — fix the claim, not the test. tools/ownership-map.mjs and playwright.config.ts are shared files: check `git status --porcelain` before staging.
